gen-dafont-nordic-fs-spline-sans: Nordic feels ancient and powerful, its closed, cramped letters spaced far apart like brush dabs. Spline Sans opens every curve wide, so paragraph after paragraph moves along in an approachable, contemporary way.
gen-dafont-nordic-fs-synonym: Synonym reads clean and dependable, its curves opened generously and its ink laid at a constant width. And once Nordic's cramped, ancient letters have spoken, paragraph after paragraph of Synonym goes down smoothly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-almendra: Almendra reads dignified and bookish, with a deep midsection in its lowercase that gives each word a settled, weighty look. Old-world gravity, carved by Nordic and settled by Almendra.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-bree-serif: Bree Serif brings literary, refined letters with outsized lowercase proportions, while Nordic's heading letters look cut out with a fixed-width router bit. Paragraphs in Bree Serif keep moving without fuss.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-quando: Quando is bookish and traditional, with sparse spacing and a big middle zone in every word. Quando carries the reading, while Nordic, all rod-stock strokes, is at its best being powerful and ancient.
gen-dafont-nulshock-fs-synonym: Stretched, outlined and bold, with a technical bite. Synonym, a sans-serif with generous openings in every curve and ink of constant thickness, gives Nulshock's wide outlines somewhere quiet to rest.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-almendra: Wide-stretched outlines, bold and technical, drawn like a fixed-width nib. Nulshock does its best work large and brief, while Almendra, dignified and bookish, takes over once the words multiply.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-bree-serif: Nulshock stretches out in wide, technical outlines with a marker-drawn plainness. Its place is big, brief wording, while Bree Serif, literary and refined with outsized lowercase proportions, covers everything else.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-quando: A rope-thin outline, stretched wide: that is Nulshock. Quando adds sparse spacing and a big middle zone in bookish, traditional serif letters, so the pairing's real strength is a technical outline meeting old-fashioned type.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-antic-slab: Oldtimer's round forms read like open parentheses, and no downstroke carries any calligraphic swell. And Antic Slab, dignified and editorial, is happy at smaller sizes, so give Oldtimer the larger sizes.
